stemBlocks.value: Make a the subject of the formula s = ut + ½at².
Think first: The term containing a is ½at², so isolate that term before undoing the ½ and the t².

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p096-q11 from workbook page 96.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract ut, multiply through by 2 to clear the half, then divide by t².

finalAnswerBlocks.value: a = 2(s − ut)/t², which can also be written a = (2s − 2ut)/t²

whyThisWorks.value: Only one term contains a, so the strategy is always the same: move every other term to the far side, then strip the coefficient off the remaining term. Multiplying by 2 clears the half and dividing by t² removes the last factor, leaving a alone.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by t² before removing ut, which drags an extra term into the fraction.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by t² before removing ut, which drags an extra term into the fraction.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing a = 2s − ut/t² and losing the bracket.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing a = 2s − ut/t² and losing the bracket.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by t instead of t².
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by t instead of t².

examTip.value: Locate the single term containing the new subject first; everything else in the formula simply has to be moved out of the way.
